Execute the supplied author's code to answer the task questions. Read /code/README.md
and /REPRODUCING.md first. The controller has already provisioned the author's image:
run commands directly inside this container, not through nested Docker. Work in /code;
data are in /data and /results starts empty. Network access is disabled. Do not alter
experimental code, hardcode answers, or use remembered/published results.
If blocked, submit null values for unanswered questions, with evidence of the blocker
and an optional explanation field. Do not invent values to complete the report. If a required
code change is necessary, explain the blocker instead of silently patching it.
Keep every response in English. Tool outputs include controller-owned artifact IDs and
1-based line numbers. Submit each question's value with evidence from THIS execution.

10: # read the csv
11: dat <- read.csv("../data/semlavaan.csv", header=TRUE, fileEncoding="CP932")
12: 
13: library(lavaan)
14: # https://lavaan.ugent.be/
15: model <- '
16: Achievement =~ Midterm + Final + Quiz
17: Proficiency =~ Exam1 + Exam2 + Exam3
18: Proficiency ~ Achievement
19: '
20: 
21: fit <- sem(model, data=dat)
22: summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
23: 
24: # Path diagram
25: library(semPlot)
26: 
27: # Standardized estimates
28: png("../results/plot1.png", width = 600, height = 600)
29: semPaths(fit, "std", style="lisrel", # LISREL style
30:          mar=c(6,1,3,1), # margin (bottom, left, up, right)
31:          edge.label.cex=.8, # font size for coefficients
32:          fade=F, # keep the arrow size the same
33:          theme="gray") # gray color
34: dev.off()

I want to make sure I capture all the relevant details in the output, as variances can be quite important. I should also ensure that the execution goes smoothly, so I'll keep an eye on the process, checking for errors along the way. Let's get that done!
